lessons.title: Mo, do, a (sé): séimhiú
lessons.rule: After mo (my), do (your) and a (his), add h after the first letter of the noun: mo theach, do chóta, a bhróga. Nouns beginning with l, n or r do not change.
steps: Find the word before the brackets: mo (my).
Add h after the first letter of the noun: guthán becomes ghuthán.
Write the sentence: Seo é mo ghuthán.

more.answer: D'ith sé a cheapaire ar an bhus.

lessons.title: M' agus d' roimh ghuta
lessons.en: My and your before a vowel
lessons.rule: Before a vowel, mo becomes m' and do becomes d', joined to the noun: m'uncail, d'athair. A noun beginning with f first takes h, then counts as a vowel: m'fhón, d'fhoirm.
steps: Add h after the f, as after any mo: fón becomes fhón.
fh makes no sound, so the word now begins with a vowel sound: mo becomes m'.
Join them and write the sentence: Seo é m'fhón póca.

lessons.hint: Vowel or fh next: m' and d', no space.

lessons.title: A (sí): h roimh ghuta
lessons.rule: After a meaning her, a consonant does not change (a cara), but a vowel takes h in front (a haintín). The same goes for lena (with her): lena haintín.
steps: Check whose it is: Síle's, so a means her.
Look at the first letter: uaireadóir begins with a vowel, so put h in front: huaireadóir.
Write the sentence: Bhris Síle a huaireadóir ag an chamógaíocht.

lessons.title: Ár, bhur, a (siad): urú
lessons.rule: After ár (our), bhur (your, plural) and a (their), eclipse the noun: mb, gc, nd, bhf, ng, bp, dt, and n- before a vowel. Nouns beginning with l, m, n, r or s do not change.
steps: Find the word before the brackets: bhur (your, plural).
Eclipse the first letter: t takes d in front, so ticéid becomes dticéid.
Write the sentence: Cá bhfuil bhur dticéid, a pháistí?

lessons.title: I mo chónaí, ina shuí
lessons.en: Saying where or how someone is: i mo chónaí
lessons.rule: To say someone lives somewhere or is sitting, standing, lying, asleep, awake or silent, use tá + i mo, i do, ina, inár or in bhur + the state word (cónaí, suí, seasamh, luí, codladh, dúiseacht, tost). Then change the state word as after the possessive: ina shuí (his), ina suí (her), ina gcodladh (their).
steps: Find the person: sé (he), so ina means his.
After his, add h after the first letter: suí becomes shuí.
Write the sentence: Tá sé ina shuí ar an bhus.

example.prompt: Tá sé ina (suí) ar an bhus.
example.answer: Tá sé ina shuí ar an bhus.

more.answer: Tá sí ina cónaí i nDún na nGall.

lessons.hint: i + possessive + state word, then the usual h, h before a vowel or eclipsis.
